newsitem.title: USA: Pentagon, corporations to pay $216 mln for cleanup.
newsitem.headline: Pentagon, corporations to pay $216 mln for cleanup.

text.p: Federal and state authorities on Tuesday announced a $221.5 million settlement, involving 90 companies and the U.S. military, to pay for the cleanup of a Superfund site here.
The Department of Defense will be the biggest contributor, paying more than $175 million.

The agreement will cover 70 percent of the $315 million the federal Environmental Protection Agency estimates it will spend on cleaning up the "toxic soup" that accumulated in the 13 acre lagoon at Bridgeport Rental and Oil Services during its three decades of operations here.
It was once the 35th site on the Superfund list.
A four-year stage of incinerating 172,000 tons of sludge and PCB-tainted soil was completed and the equipment dismantled earlier this year. The next stage is to remedy groundwater contamination.

A consent order filed in federal court in Camden said corporations such as DuPont, Monsanto, Ciba-Geigy, Rohm and Haas, Dow Chemical Co, Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Mobil Corp and SmithKline Beecham will share in a $46 million settlement. The proportion paid by each was sealed by the court.
